summary.text: The atlas recommends testing first sixteen targets that no drug treats in UC, four from each list of targets without therapy: first-in-class SDR16C5, CYP4X1, CPXM1 and CHRDL2; well known without a drug SERPINB5, CXCL1, CHI3L1 and REG1B; repurposing INHBA, CFB, LY96 and SELP; and genetics first TUFM, CEBPB, FIGNL1 and CFAP90. Each was chosen from the most robust genes of its list and is argued on its direction, its cell, its drug route, its safety and its first experiment.

SERPINB5 has the most complete case: epithelial cells make almost all of it in all four atlases, its rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]), and two mouse studies report that knockdown or ablation protected against colitis. Its weak points are that both studies date from 2026 and that its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled: UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor, while a study of IBD tissue linked its aberrant expression with neoplastic transformation.

The first-in-class choices are changes of the lining or the stroma that survive the composition adjustment, such as SDR16C5 (retained fraction [gene=SDR16C5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.66]), but the literature reviews found no functional study of any of them, and several genes of that pool were set aside because their rise mostly reports cells arriving: LILRA1 and CEACAM4 are neutrophil transcripts and PCDH17 keeps only [gene=PCDH17; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.098] of its rise.

For the repurposing targets an inhibitor already exists for another disease, but the data argue for caution: INHBA and SELP separate ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, so they mark severity, and for CFB a loss-of-function variant implies its function protects. Genetics gives the strongest causal argument for TUFM, whose higher expression in colon raises UC risk (odds ratio per SD [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.191]), although biopsies show no rise; the other genetics-first genes rest on sequence predictions. These are hypotheses from public data, to be tested in human cells first.

expression.text: The largest and most consistent increases in UC mucosa are remodelling, antimicrobial and neutrophil genes. CHI3L1 [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913] and MMP3 [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822] are among the largest pooled increases of all genes up in the eight-cohort meta-analysis, and DUOX2 [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033] and CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687] are also up in all eight cohorts.

Epithelial metabolism is lost. AQP8 has the largest pooled loss of all genes down in the meta-analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633] and falls in all eight cohorts, and HMGCS2 is among the largest losses. The loss of the epithelial transporter SLC26A2 stays significant after composition adjustment [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], a change of the tissue itself.

JAK2 is up in all eight cohorts but only modestly [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833]; it has the second highest Open Targets association with UC among the genes in this atlas's graph, so its place among the candidates comes from genetics and drug history rather than expression.

inflammation.text: Most leading changes are local to inflamed mucosa. Comparing inflamed with non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients (GSE193677), CXCR2 rises [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972] with only a small change in non-inflamed versus control mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]; CD274 behaves the same way ([gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.0008] against [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]), and HMGCS2 is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so its loss belongs to inflammation.
MMP3, DUOX2, TREM1 and AQP9 are also higher in inflamed than in non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients.

replication.text: The leading changes reproduce across cohorts: CXCR2, CHI3L1, DUOX2, JAK2 and AQP8 are significant in the same direction in all eight cohorts. At protein level, in an independent proteomics study, IDO1 [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917] and HMGCS2 [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094] change in the same direction as RNA, whereas CHI3L1 rises much less as protein [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and was not called significant by the authors.

literature.text: The curated corpus holds no verbatim-checked CXCR2 relation, a limit of the corpus rather than of the field: Europe PMC returns [gene=CXCR2; type=mouse_colitis_literature; source=DATASET:EUROPEPMC_MOUSE; mouse_colitis_papers=19] mouse colitis papers on CXCR2. Among the corpus abstracts, a Mendelian randomisation, colocalisation and transcriptomic study proposes CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC, although in its Mendelian randomisation higher CXCR1 and CXCR2 expression went with lower UC risk (this atlas has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument to check it), and another ties the CXCL5 to CXCR2 axis to neutrophil chemotaxis. The cited IDO1 support is one experimental study: IDO1 was elevated in UC patients, was linked in colitis mice to pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation through the GRP78-XBP1 pathway, and an IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis.

For biomarkers the literature is more useful. MMP1 is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with the modified Mayo score, Geboes score and Robarts Histopathology Index; CHI3L1 is upregulated in UC and promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1 and NF-kappaB; DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated in inflamed UC biopsies; and HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC.

The CXCL8 axis with its receptors is described as taking part in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, and in a blood RNA-seq validation set CXCL8 was among the best diagnostic genes for IBD, second to ITGA5, an IBD-level rather than UC-specific result. CXCL1 is nominated as a diagnostic or activity marker in several bioinformatic studies; alone it is only a fair activity marker, and its high accuracy comes within a combined multi-gene model.

IL1B is listed among credible diagnostic biomarkers for UC, and in a tofacitinib study non-responders showed expansion and activation of macrophages and fibroblasts after treatment, with upregulation of MMP9, IL1B, IL6, CXCL1, CXCL8 and S100A9 versus baseline: a non-response signature of infiltrating immune cells rather than of epithelial change.

external.text: Approved-target genetics behaves as a positive control. IL12B carries a strong Open Targets genetic association with UC [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and is the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation result among this atlas's genes: genetically higher protein raises UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], the signal colocalises with an IBD GWAS locus and replicates in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction.

Among expression-led candidates, genetics often points the other way. For CD274 higher plasma protein lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595] although it rises in inflamed mucosa, which suggests a compensatory rise. CXCL5 is also protective in plasma [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634] but rests on a tag variant without colocalisation. SLC26A3 falls in inflamed mucosa, yet higher expression in IBDverse crypt progenitors raises UC risk [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]. CXCL8 is null in plasma (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) and has no Open Targets genetic association.

CXCR2 has a high Open Targets genetic association score but no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so Mendelian randomisation could not test it. Two antagonists were tested in UC, SB-656933 and navarixin (SCH-527123, also coded MK-7123), and neither went beyond phase 2, the highest UC stage recorded; reparixin reached phase 3 outside UC (type I diabetes and COVID-19 in the record). Navarixin itself, as MK-7123, caused a dose-dependent decrease in absolute neutrophil count in a COPD trial, with discontinuations at higher doses. Mouse colitis papers include a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no single-gene colitis phenotype for it.

Among the JAK kinases the human genetic support sits on JAK2 (Open Targets genetic association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]), with TYK2 lower [gene=TYK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.2863] and JAK1 none [gene=JAK1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.0]; JAK2 and TYK2 carry the interleukin-23 receptor signal, which links this control to IL12B. The JAK inhibitors that worked in UC trials are tofacitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor that, like the others, inhibits JAK1-dependent pathways most potently but acts more than filgotinib on JAK2- and JAK3-dependent ones, upadacitinib, a selective JAK1 inhibitor, and filgotinib, a JAK1-preferential inhibitor: the JAK1-selective drugs worked too, so the trials do not show that JAK2 blockade is needed, although JAK1 has no genetic association here, and JAK2 also carries erythropoietin and thrombopoietin receptor signals. Within TYK2, the selective deucravacitinib did not show significant benefit over placebo in UC phase 2, whereas brepocitinib, a TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor, was more effective than placebo in UC phase 2b. The JAK2 result therefore supports the JAK class as a positive control, not a JAK2-selective drug.

cells.text: Neutrophil genes lead the ranking but report cell arrival. In Gubatan 2026 neutrophils make most CXCR2 [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965], CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] and TREM1 [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894] transcripts. Smillie 2019 has [type=sc_atlas; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_cell_types=0] neutrophil cell types among its [type=sc_atlas; source=DATASET:SCP259; n_cell_types=51], so it attributes CXCR2 to the few T/NK cells that express it, and that attribution does not replicate in the other atlases. After composition adjustment CXCL8 loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]) and CXCR2 keeps only a small change [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409].

Two increases are changes of the tissue itself. DUOX2 is made by enterocytes [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] and MMP1 by inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]; both attributions replicate in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, and both keep a clear adjusted change ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] and [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]). The loss of SLC26A2 is intrinsic [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], with almost no neutrophil contribution [gene=SLC26A2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.014].

IDO1, CHI3L1 and CD274 have mixed sources. IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie 2019 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026; CHI3L1 is stromal in Smillie 2019 but myeloid in Gubatan 2026, where neutrophils also contribute [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]; CD274 is myeloid-dominant but diffuse, with a large neutrophil share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. All three keep a significant change after adjustment ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]); the composition model can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so these are partly tissue changes.

spatial.text: In deconvolved Visium spots inflammatory fibroblasts give the largest in-situ contribution to MMP1 [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568], and the spots with high MMP1 are enriched in inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils around them, so tissue and single-cell data agree. CosMx detects MMP1 only at background.
DUOX2 is placed in epithelium by both Xenium and Visium, in agreement with its enterocyte source in the single-cell atlases.

pathways.text: Pathway activity rises broadly in inflamed mucosa. NFkB and TNFa activity are up in all eight cohorts, the NFkB t reaching [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79] in GSE206285, and JAK-STAT, TGFb, EGFR, MAPK, PI3K and Hypoxia are also up in all eight, WNT in seven. STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6], as is AP1. Because so many pathways rise together these signals are robust but not specific, and VEGF and Androgen are not consistent across cohorts.

The most specific circuit is neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2: in Gubatan 2026 the link from the Neutrophil CXCR4 state to the Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed mucosa, a feed-forward recruitment loop, and neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 endothelium. Inflammatory fibroblasts send CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils at much lower scores, IL1B mainly reaches IL1R2 on neutrophil states, and the expected neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

Of the circuit genes, CXCR2 has recorded antagonists, of which reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 are also listed against CXCR1, IL1B has canakinumab, approved outside IBD (cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome in the record), and TREM1 has nangibotide in phase 2; no drug is recorded for CXCL1 or CXCL5.

treatment.text: Gene-level non-response signals are severity markers. Higher baseline CXCR2 (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]), CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and IL11 ([gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]) are associated with ustekinumab non-response, but each also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126], [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154], [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234], [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]). OSM ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) is not significant in the UNIFI placebo arm ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), yet the drug-by-placebo interaction is not significant either ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.974]), so drug specificity is not shown.

At pathway level TNFa is higher in ustekinumab non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and in several other arms including UNIFI placebo, so it is a severity axis; it is not significant in PURSUIT placebo ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]) or the PROTECT mesalazine arm ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]). TGFb behaves the same ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]; UNIFI placebo [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]). Target expression does not stratify response: IL12B ([gene=IL12B; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.84]) and IL23A ([gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) for ustekinumab, and ITGB7 for vedolizumab ([gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]). In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 has the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates of the discovery screen and is up in [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7] cohorts. Its transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts, and the other single-cell atlases agree [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; other_atlases_agreeing=3]. The increase is partly composition, an antibody is the predicted modality, and no response or functional data exist.

CPXM1 has the second largest increase of the first-in-class candidates. It is stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026, its increase is partly composition, and genetics and response data are missing.

XKR9 keeps the highest share of its change after composition adjustment among the first-in-class candidates and is one of four epithelial candidates classed intrinsic, but it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts, the second fewest of the candidates.

GLT1D1, another first-in-class candidate, is composition-driven: neutrophils make most of its RNA in inflamed mucosa (share [gene=GLT1D1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.891]) and its myeloid lineage replicates in all three other atlases, so its rise reflects infiltrating neutrophils rather than a change of the tissue itself.

integration.text: The streams agree on a core picture. Expression, the paired inflamed and non-inflamed data, the pathway layer and single cells point to a neutrophil-rich inflamed mucosa with NFkB, TNFa and STAT3 activity, with AQP8 showing the largest pooled loss, and the treatment data show that the same neutrophil signals mark severity in drug and placebo arms alike. Genetics and drug history agree for IL12B, and for JAK2 at the level of the JAK class; both have strong Open Targets genetic association with UC ([gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]).

They disagree on causality. CXCL8 and CHI3L1, among the largest pooled increases, have no Open Targets genetic association, and CXCL8 is null in plasma Mendelian randomisation, so they read as consequences of inflammation and as biomarkers. For CD274 and CXCL5 genetics runs opposite to an inhibitor, since higher plasma protein lowers risk, and for SLC26A3 the gut eQTL direction is opposite to its loss in biopsies. This atlas has no instrument to test CXCR2 by Mendelian randomisation; one published study found higher CXCR1 and CXCR2 expression with lower UC risk, the direction opposite to an antagonist.

decision.text: From the first-in-class pool, XKR9 keeps most of its rise after the composition adjustment (retained fraction [gene=XKR9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.798]) but is up in only four of eight cohorts and two of three other atlases. LILRA1 and CEACAM4 mostly report neutrophil arrival (neutrophil shares [gene=LILRA1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.502] and [gene=CEACAM4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.87]), and PCDH17 keeps only [gene=PCDH17; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.098] of its rise, a marker of vascular or stromal expansion. LAIR2 is a T/NK transcript whose change is in large part T-cell influx. OLFML2B is attributed to the same lineage in only one of three other atlases, LYPD5 has no UC or IBD paper, and FJX1's only colitis-model paper concerns tumours, not inflammation; SGIP1 and FIBIN are stromal genes whose rise is mostly composition. PCDH17's baseline level is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=PCDH17; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000594]) but also with corticosteroid non-response and faecal calprotectin, which points to inflammation burden; LAIR2 rises in inflamed mucosa ([gene=LAIR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.3277]) but not in non-inflamed mucosa, and LILRA1 likewise ([gene=LILRA1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.3307]), both signals of inflammation rather than of the tissue.

From the well-known pool, MMP10 is a replicated biomarker, but MMP10-deficient mice had worse DSS colitis, so blocking it may impair healing. CXCL3 reaches neutrophil CXCR2 like CXCL1 and shares its receptor, so the data do not single it out over CXCL1. KLK10 and PDPN rise mostly through changes in cell proportions.

From the repurposing pool, GUCY1A1 was not chosen: its inhibitor is recorded for colorectal neoplasms rather than an inflammatory disease, and loss of the gene causes Moyamoya disease, so long-term inhibition carries a vascular risk.

From the genetics-first pool, RORC was not chosen. Its risk allele lowers expression, so the hypothesis is to restore it, but no record names a way to raise it with a drug, its mRNA loss in inflamed mucosa is small and not local to inflammation (paired change [gene=RORC; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-0.0627]), and its regulon activity is inferred up in inflamed mucosa, which weighs against restoring it.

targets.rationale: Direction: inhibit; SDR16C5 rises in UC in seven of eight cohorts. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make it (transit-amplifying, cycling and immature goblet cells), the lineage agrees in all three other atlases, and the rise is intrinsic, with a retained fraction of [gene=SDR16C5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.66] after the composition adjustment, so it is a change of the lining itself. Drug route: Open Targets predicts it tractable. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events; it has never been tested in mouse colitis. First experiment: silencing in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa, as proposed on the card. What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence; its only UC paper names it in a list.

Direction: inhibit; CYP4X1 rises in UC in all eight cohorts. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make it, the lineage agrees in all three other atlases, and its rise is classed intrinsic after the composition adjustment, so it is a change of the lining. Drug route: Open Targets predicts both an antibody and a small-molecule route. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events; it has never been tested in mouse colitis. First experiment: silencing or inhibition in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa. What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence; its only UC paper names it in a list.

Direction: inhibit; CPXM1 rises in UC with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CPXM1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.8968], significant in seven of eight cohorts, and is already raised in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=CPXM1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.0059]), so it tracks the disease, not only local inflammation. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts make it (stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, epithelial in Gubatan 2026), and part of the rise survives the composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.057]). Drug route: an antibody is the predicted modality. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events. First experiment: blocking or silencing it in primary fibroblasts from inflamed UC mucosa. What is missing: plasma Mendelian randomisation is not significant, it has never been tested in mouse colitis, and its literature is one expression paper.

Direction: inhibit; CHRDL2 rises in UC in seven of eight cohorts. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts make it (stromal share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]) and the lineage agrees in all three other atlases, but only part of the rise survives the composition adjustment (retained fraction [gene=CHRDL2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.276]), and Visium places its in-situ signal in smooth muscle, so the producing cell is not settled. Drug route: it is secreted and a predicted antibody target; UniProt describes it as a possible inhibitor of BMP activity. Safety: not loss-constrained, no recorded safety events. Its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, so it marks severity. First experiment: a blocking antibody on inflamed UC fibroblasts. What is missing: genetics (plasma Mendelian randomisation not significant) and any mouse colitis study.

Direction: inhibit; SERPINB5 rises in all eight cohorts, by [gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.0451] log2 units in inflamed against non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make almost all of it (share [gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.953]), in all four atlases, and the rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]). Function: two 2026 mouse studies report that knockdown or ablation protected against colitis, which is the strongest functional support in the pool, though both date from 2026. Drug route: Open Targets predicts an antibody and a small-molecule route. Safety: it is not loss-constrained. UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor, but a study of IBD tissue linked its aberrant expression with disease activity and neoplastic transformation and proposed targeting it for control of disease activity and cancer prophylaxis, so its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled and long-term inhibition still needs care. First experiment: silencing in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa stimulated with TNF.

Direction: inhibit; CXCL1 rises across cohorts with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CXCL1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.6892]. Cell and tissue: in Gubatan 2026 single cells inflammatory fibroblasts send it to CXCR2 on neutrophils and to ACKR1 on endothelium, and UniProt records its chemotactic activity for neutrophils; most of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions, so blocking it would act on neutrophil recruitment rather than on a change of the tissue. Drug route: secreted, a predicted antibody target, with no drug against CXCL1 itself. Safety: not loss-constrained, no recorded safety events. First experiment: a neutralising antibody in a co-culture of inflamed UC fibroblasts with blood neutrophils, reading neutrophil migration. Caveat: the circuit is co-expression, not proof of signalling, and plasma Mendelian randomisation is not significant.

Direction: inhibit, with a caution. CHI3L1 has one of the largest increases (inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=3.8187], up in all eight cohorts) and its protein rises too (log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]), which makes it a marker first. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts make it in Smillie 2019, but neutrophils make a large share in Gubatan 2026, and part of the rise survives adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]). Function: an anti-CHI3L1 antibody reduced DSS colitis, but knockout mice develop more severe colitis, so blocking it could harm the epithelium. Drug route: secreted, predicted antibody and small-molecule target. Genetics: plasma and colon Mendelian randomisation are not significant. First experiment: a blocking antibody on inflamed UC fibroblasts and on epithelial organoids in parallel, to see benefit and harm in one test.

Direction: inhibit, as a hypothesis to test. REG1B is epithelial in all four atlases and its rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC [gene=REG1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.4585]). Literature: it is supported as a biomarker (a hub gene of UC progression, a diagnostic-model gene and a predictor of relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal), with no functional study in either direction, and its baseline level does not separate responders in any drug arm. Drug route: secreted, a predicted antibody target. Safety: not loss-constrained, no recorded safety events, but UniProt links it with regeneration, so blocking it could slow repair. First experiment: a functional test first, silencing or adding the protein in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa, before any antibody.

Direction: inhibit; INHBA (activin A) rises with a pooled log2FC of [gene=INHBA; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.6188]. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts and macrophages make it and the lineage does not replicate across atlases; part of the rise survives adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=INHBA; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.6949]). Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension and was never tried in UC or IBD. Literature: it was overexpressed in baseline biopsies of patients who failed anti-TNF therapy, but in this atlas it separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, so it marks severity. Safety: it is strongly loss-constrained (LOEUF [gene=INHBA; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=0.166]). In experimental colitis, administration of follistatin attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, which supports blocking activin signalling. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on inflamed UC fibroblasts and macrophages, then on explants of inflamed mucosa.

Direction: inhibit, against a contrary signal. CFB rises with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CFB; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.24], significant in seven of eight cohorts, its protein rises too, and epithelial cells make it as an intrinsic change (adjusted log2FC [gene=CFB; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8989]). Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for IgA glomerulonephritis and paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria and was never tried in UC. Against it: a CFB loss-of-function variant linked to perianal Crohn's disease implies its function protects, the treatment arms show no response signal, and loss of the gene causes complement factor B deficiency, so long-term inhibition may reproduce that disease. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on organoids and explants of inflamed UC mucosa, reading epithelial damage as well as inflammation.

Direction: inhibit, with a caution. LY96 (MD-2) is associated with ustekinumab non-response while the UNIFI placebo arm is not significant (padj [gene=LY96; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.144]). Cell: neutrophils make much of its RNA, so its rise reports in part cell arrival. Drug route: an inhibitor reached phase 3 in sepsis and covid-19 and was never tried in UC. Literature: in mice, TLR4/MD-2 blockade inhibited colitis-associated neoplasia and an MD-2 binder alleviated TNBS colitis, but another anti-TLR4/MD-2 antibody interfered with mucosal healing during recovery. Genetics: plasma and gut-cell Mendelian randomisation are not significant. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on inflamed UC explants, read early and during recovery.

Direction: inhibit; SELP (P-selectin) rises in inflamed mucosa (inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=SELP; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.8372] against [gene=SELP; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.4546] in non-inflamed mucosa), so it is a local-inflammation signal. Cell: endothelium sends it to SELPLG on neutrophils, and UniProt describes it as the receptor that binds activated endothelium or platelets to leukocytes. Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for sickle cell anaemia and was never tried in UC. Against it: plasma Mendelian randomisation is null (p [gene=SELP; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.484]) and its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, and in experimental colitis an anti-P-selectin antibody did not significantly improve colitis. The reviewer is against testing it first; it stays as the last repurposing choice because the only other gene of the pool, GUCY1A1, carries a vascular risk, and the negative animal result argues for a human test before any trial. First experiment: the existing antibody in a flow assay of neutrophils over inflamed UC endothelial cells.

Direction: inhibit; the UC risk allele raises TUFM expression, and Mendelian randomisation agrees: higher expression in sigmoid colon raises UC risk (odds ratio per SD [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.191]), colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen and Liu 2023, and so does expression in gut plasma B cells ([gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.356]). This is the strongest causal evidence in the pool. Cell and tissue: the predicted effect is largest in blood neutrophils, while single cells place it in plasma and epithelial cells, and in inflamed MSCCR biopsies it is slightly lower, not higher (log2FC [gene=TUFM; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.188]), with no change in non-inflamed mucosa, which does not support the inhibition hypothesis in tissue. Drug route and safety: TUFM is a ubiquitous mitochondrial gene, so a drug would need to act in one cell type. First experiment: allele-specific silencing in gut plasma cells or neutrophils. Caveat: one instrument. The reviewer is against testing it first for these reasons; it stays because it carries the only causal genetic support in the pool, and the first experiment tests that support in one cell type before any drug is considered.

Direction: inhibit; the risk allele raises CEBPB, predicted in colon dendritic cells, and its mRNA rises in biopsies (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CEBPB; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.27]), with its regulon active in all cohorts. Cell: it is a broadly expressed transcription factor, made mostly by neutrophils and macrophages (neutrophil share [gene=CEBPB; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.698]), and the predicted dendritic cell is not the main source. Against it: gut-cell Mendelian randomisation points the other way without reaching significance, and its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike. Drug route: a transcription factor is hard to drug, though nintedanib alleviated DSS colitis in mice by inhibiting CEBPB signalling. First experiment: silencing in monocyte-derived dendritic cells carrying the risk allele.

Direction: inhibit; the risk allele is predicted to raise FIGNL1 in colon NK cells, in a confidently fine-mapped UC signal. Against it: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change. It stays in the decision because the genetics list has only five candidates and its prediction is confident; it is a hypothesis about inherited risk, not about inflamed tissue. The reviewer is against it; it stays because the rule takes four genes from each list and the remaining genetics candidate, RORC, has data against its direction. First experiment: allele-specific expression and silencing in primary NK cells.

Direction: inhibit; the risk allele is predicted to raise CFAP90 in colon goblet cells and several blood cell types, in a confidently fine-mapped UC signal. Against it: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies. Like FIGNL1, it is a hypothesis about inherited risk; the first step is to confirm the predicted effect of the variant on expression in goblet cells before any functional test. The reviewer is against it for the same reasons as FIGNL1, and it stays for the same reason.

limitations.text: Bulk changes of neutrophil and myeloid genes are confounded by cell influx; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so retained fractions are approximate.
Co-expression of ligand and receptor in single cells is not proof of signalling.
The plasma IL12B protein measure (UKB-PPP) does not separate IL-12, IL-23 and free p40, so the Mendelian randomisation result supports the IL-12/IL-23 axis, not anti-p40 over anti-p19 blockade.
Neutrophils also take part in mucosal repair, so blocking their recruitment could slow healing as well as reduce inflammation; CXCR2 antagonists have not gone beyond phase 2 in UC.
Several leading candidates (CXCR2, CXCR1, JAK2) have no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so their causal direction is untested rather than refuted.

The decision is the orchestrator's judgement, a language model, within a fixed rule; the choice between genes of similar evidence (for example XKR9 against CHRDL2) could go either way, and the not-chosen genes of each pool are listed with the reason.
The specialists examined the pool genes their tools cover within a call budget; CYP4X1, KLK10, PDPN, GUCY1A1 and several first-in-class genes were judged on their list records alone.

The data sections of this report (expression, inflammation, replication, literature, external, cells, spatial, pathways, treatment, discovery, integration) were written for the run of 2026-11-27 from its verified agent files and were verified and read again in this run; the summary, the decision and the targets are new.

The expert review of this run was made by Claude Sonnet: the Opus 5.5 reviewer was stopped twice by the model's safeguards. The review can be redone on the same input without re-running the specialists.
A reading subagent checked every claim against its cited records; claims it found unsupported are listed in the Agents tab rather than removed.
